outlooks.summary: Severe storms are likely across parts of the Southern Plains today, with damaging wind, hail, and a couple tornadoes possible. Scattered strong to severe storms are also possible across a broader area from the central and southern Plains eastward to the mid Mississippi Valley. A more isolated severe risk extends into the southern Great Lakes, Ohio and Tennessee Valleys and Southeast.

sections.title: Southern and Central Plains
sections.text: An upper-level trough will move into the High Plains today as southwest mid-level flow remains over much of the south-central U.S. At the surface, a cold front will move southeastward into western Oklahoma and northwest Texas by early afternoon. Ahead of the front, surface dewpoints will be in the lower to mid 70s F. This will likely result in strong destabilization by afternoon across much of the warm sector. As low-level convergence increases along the front, cell initiation appears likely during the mid afternoon. Storms should initially be discrete but eventually should organize into a line segment, moving southeastward across southern and eastern Oklahoma into north Texas during the late afternoon and early evening. RAP forecast soundings ahead of the front from near Wichita Falls, Texas eastward across southern Oklahoma show MLCAPE values reaching the 3500 to 5000 J/kg range and have moderate deep-layer shear profiles. 0-6 km shear of 35 to 40 kt and 700 to 500 mb lapse rates near 8.0 C/km will be favorable for supercells with large hail during the first couple hours after initiation. As storm coverage increases ahead of the front, linear organization seems most likely sugges

sections.title: Lower Missouri Valley/Mid Mississippi Valley
sections.text: Southwest mid-level flow will be in place across the mid Mississippi Valley today as low amplitude shortwave troughs move northeastward across the region. At the surface, a cold front is forecast to advance southeastward into northwestern Missouri. A corridor of moderate instability may develop ahead of the front from south-central Missouri into southern Illinois by early afternoon. The MCS track during the early morning hours will determine where the axis of strongest instability sets up today, suggesting uncertainty exists concerning the scenario. The current thinking is that cells will initiate along an outflow boundary left over from the MCS in southwest Missouri with a cluster of storms moving eastward into the mid Mississippi Valley during the mid to late afternoon. In addition to the instability, moderate deep-layer shear is forecast across much of the region, suggesting that severe storms will be possible. Wind damage and isolated large hail will be the primary threats. The wind-damage threat may continue into the early evening especially if a cold pool can organize.

sections.title: Southeast
sections.text: An upper-level ridge will move eastward across the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys today. At the surface, a moist airmass will be in place across much of the southeastern U.S. with surface dewpoints in the mid 60s to near 70 F. In response, moderate instability appears likely to develop across much of the region by afternoon. Thunderstorms that can initiate along pre-existing outflow boundaries may develop an isolated severe threat. Wind damage will be possible with the stronger multicells near peak heating. ..Broyles/Cook.. 06/23/2019

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms should be most concentrated and intense today over parts of southern Oklahoma and north Texas into the Arklatex region and nearby Arkansas. Damaging hail, severe gusts and a few tornadoes are possible.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: An uncommonly active upper-air pattern for its latitude and time of year, around summer solstice, is in place over the CONUS. The most relevant feature is a strong mid/upper-level shortwave trough -- now apparent in moisture-channel imagery from southern WY through a vorticity max over northern CO, then southward across parts of NM. This trough will move eastward to the central/southern High Plains by 00Z, then by the end of the period, extend near an axis from the FSD/SUX vicinity to MKC, FSM and ACT. Surface analysis showed a low over northeastern OK with outflow- reinforced cold front southwestward across central/southwestern OK to near CDS, PVW and southeastern NM. The low should move northeastward into rain-cooled air over parts of eastern KS/western MO, while the cold front travels southeastward to southern OK and northwest TX by 00Z. An extensive/wavy outflow boundary, reinforced by multiple rounds of convection the past couple days, was analyzed from northern FL across south-central AL to northeastern AR, arching around central and western AR to northeastern OK and southeastern KS, where it was being overtaken by another MCS. This boundary should act as an effective warm fr

sections.title: Southern Plains...Arklatex
sections.text: An ongoing area of convection from southeastern KS to central/ southwestern OK may pose additional severe potential for a few more hours as it crosses mainly northern/central OK -- especially any convection that can remain along/ahead of the front and on the warm side of the aggregate outflow boundary, with access to surface-based effective-inflow parcels. Please refer to the remainder of SPC severe thunderstorm watches 431/432 and accompanying mesoscale discussions for near-term details. Both in the near term and through the afternoon, any relatively discrete cells forming in the warm sector over portions of eastern OK and AR may pose a short-lived tornado threat as they cross the outflow boundary, where backed flow enhances low-level hodograph size, and convection temporarily encounters a related vorticity-rich environment in the boundary layer. Additional convection is expected to develop near the front as it moves southeastward into a very favorably destabilizing air mass across southern OK and north TX today, including a few supercells with large/damaging hail possible. The preconvective warm sector will be characterized by steep low/middle-level lapse rates overlying rich bou

sections.title: South-central High Plains
sections.text: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms, including a supercell or two, may develop in a swath from the eastern Raton Mesa area of northeastern NM across eastern CO/western KS this afternoon, moving eastward to western KS and the OK/northern TX Panhandles for a few hours of severe potential. The main threats will be large hail and strong-severe gusts from any sustained and relatively discrete cells. As the mid/upper trough and embedded vorticity max approach the High Plains this afternoon, sufficient airmass recovery for surface-based convection is forecast behind the front and the morning clouds/convection. Residual moisture, with surface dew points generally in the upper 40s to mid 50s F, combined with afternoon insolation and DCVA-related cooling aloft, should support steep low/middle-level lapse rates with MLCAPE in the 500-1000 J/kg range, amidst little or no MLCINH. The deep-layer flow will be nearly unidirectional, but with favorable speed shear for organized convection. ..Edwards/Mosier.. 06/23/2019

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms should be most concentrated today over parts of southern Oklahoma, north Texas, and western Arkansas. Damaging hail, severe gusts and isolated tornadoes are possible.

sections.title: Southern Plains
sections.text: Water vapor imagery shows an upper trough axis over the southern Rockies, with broad cyclonic flow aloft over the southern high Plains. A large and well-organized MCS is sagging east-southeastward across parts of OK/AR, with a slow weakening trend noted over southern OK. This activity may re-intensify this afternoon as it moves into an increasingly warm/unstable air mass over AR. Damaging winds along the leading edge of the convection will be the main threat. These storms could maintain intensity as far southeast as west TN and northern MS this evening. Farther southwest, strong heating will lead to a very unstable air mass over northwest TX later today. Splitting supercell thunderstorm development is expected to occur near the surface triple-point west of ABI, with storms expanding eastward across north TX and southern OK. Initial storms will pose a risk of very large hail and a tornado or two. Storms should grow upscale by early evening, with bowing structures and a damaging wind threat moving across much of the ENH risk area.

sections.title: IL/IN/KY
sections.text: A remnant MCV is noted over the STL area, with an associated line of thunderstorms extending across southern IL. These storms are moving into a moist and moderately unstable air mass, where sufficient vertical shear is present for convective organization. Multicell and bowing structures are expected to affect this region this afternoon, with a risk of locally damaging wind gusts. ..Hart/Karstens.. 06/23/2019

outlooks.summary: Strong/severe thunderstorms will continue over parts of southern Oklahoma, north Texas, and western Arkansas, and in a less-widespread nature over adjacent/surrounding areas. Damaging hail, severe gusts and a tornado or two are possible. A few severe storms will also occur from the lower and middle Ohio Valley southward into the Southeast, and a severe storm or two will remain possible over portions of the central high Plains area.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: Convective evolution remains largely as anticipated this afternoon, thus requiring few substantive changes to the outlook at this time. Along with some eastward expansion of the risk areas over the mid Ohio Valley area where a rather fast-moving band of storms has developed, the most substantial change is the addition of a SLGT risk area across Georgia, within the broader area of MRGL risk. Here, weakly organized but fairly widespread storms -- the stronger of which will pose risk for brief/locally damaging winds -- warrants an increase in wind probability this afternoon. For additional short-term information regarding the Georgia risk, please refer to recently issued MCD #1219. ..Goss.. 06/23/2019 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1111 AM CDT Sun Jun 23 2019/

outlooks.summary: Strong/severe thunderstorms associated with wind damage and hail will continue over parts of north Texas into parts of the Arklatex this evening. A few severe storms will also occur in the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys with a severe storm or two also possible in the central High Plains.

sections.title: Southern Plains/Arklatex/Lower Mississippi Valley
sections.text: The latest water vapor imagery shows an upper-level trough in the High Plains with west-southwesterly mid-level flow over the southern Plains and Arklatex. At the surface, a cold front is located from west-central Texas to near the Red River and eastward into southern Arkansas. A linear MCS is currently ongoing just to the south of the front. A very moist airmass is located to the south of the MCS with surface dewpoints in the mid 70s F. This is contributing to strong instability with MLCAPE values estimated to be from 3000 to 4500 J/kg by the RAP and confirmed by the 00Z sounding at Forth Worth. That sounding also shows 0-6 km near 35 kt with a steep mid-level lapse rate. Deep-layer shear is likely stronger to the west across much of north Texas where supercells with very large hail will be possible early this evening. As the linear MCS continues to advance south-southeastward across north and northeast Texas into southwest Arkansas, wind damage will be likely with the stronger portions of the line...see MCD 436. The line should gradually weaken later this evening as it moves into parts of east Texas and northern Louisiana.

sections.title: Northern Texas Panhandle, Oklahoma Panhandle/Kansas
sections.text: A few isolated thunderstorms are currently ongoing ahead of an upper-level trough from the northern Texas Panhandle into central Kansas. These storms are located in a weakly unstable airmass with surface dewpoints in the lower to mid 50s F. In spite of this, the RAP is showing moderate deep-layer shear from the southern High Plains northeastward into the central Plains along the northern edge of a mid-level jet max. This will continue to support isolated severe storm development early this evening. Marginally severe wind gusts and hail will be the primary threats.

sections.title: Ohio and Tennessee Valleys
sections.text: A line of thunderstorms is currently ongoing along an outflow boundary from western Kentucky southwestward into northern Mississippi. A moist and unstable airmass is located ahead of the line where low-level level lapse rates are steep. This will be sufficient for isolated damaging wind gusts with the stronger portions of the line early this evening. A few severe storms with isolated damaging wind gusts will also be possible ahead of the line across eastern Kentucky and northward into western Indiana early this evening. The line should eventually weaken as it moves eastward into the southern Appalachians and into the central Gulf Coast states later this evening. ..Broyles.. 06/24/2019

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Damaging wind gusts and isolated hail remain possible across southeast KS and north-central OK. A downstream watch is being considered for southwest MO and far northwest AR.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Bowing line segment moving eastward at about 40 kt across southeast KS has recently shown increased forward progression as well as a more organized reflectivity structure. That being said, the air mass ahead of the line is characterized by temperatures in the mid/upper 60s, dewpoints in the low/mid 60s, and a deep stable layer due to persistent precipitation. As a result, despite the favorable reflectivity and velocity signatures, the elevated nature of this bow and stable low-levels will likely limit the realization of strong wind gusts at the surface. Farther south, the cold pool continues to surge southeastward, with much of the thunderstorm activity displaced north of this boundary. A recent gust of 47 kt was reported in El Reno as the gust front moved through. A few stronger updrafts do exist near Logan, Payne, and Noble Counties in north-central OK, near the intersection with the remnant outflow boundary. Isolated hail and occasional strong gusts remain possible along this progressive gust front.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A localized risk for strong winds remains across valid portions of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 432, however a downstream watch is not anticipated in the near term.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A small bowing segment with a history of damaging winds was located across far northwest Arkansas at 1500Z. As this severe thunderstorm moves east over the next couple of hours it will encounter boundary layer air stabilized by prior convection, and the wind damage potential is expected to become increasingly limited in the near term. Farther southwest, thunderstorms were largely elevated behind the southward-sagging cold pool, with no recent severe weather reports. Some diurnal intensification is expected by this afternoon as the cold pool continues moving south into a very unstable but increasingly weaker-shear environment. Although a downstream watch is not anticipated in the near term, one will likely be needed by early-mid afternoon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms are expected to increase in intensity this afternoon with a risk for damaging winds and isolated large hail. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be issued soon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A linear convective system extended from southeast MO southwest across southeast OK at 1720Z, with localized near severe winds reported from the northern portion where a bowing structure was noted. Downstream, ample daytime heating continues and MLCAPE values generally range between 2000 and 3000 J/kg, with additional destabilization expected. As the convective line, with a well-established cold pool in its wake, continues southeast this afternoon, subtle strengthening of deep-layer shear should contribute to intensifying updrafts along the leading edge, with additional storm development possible in advance of the line. Linear/bowing segments will remain the primary mode, with multicell and supercell structures possible with the more isolated cells. Damaging winds and instances of large hail will be the primary severe hazards. Transient areas of low-level rotation and perhaps a brief tornado will also be possible. Given these expected developments, a Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed soon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Potential for ongoing convection to intensify within increasingly unstable airmass. Area being monitored for possible watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Regional radar trends show a persistent trailing stratiform MCS moving northeast, now crossing into southern portions of Indiana. Visible satellite shows the area downstream of this MCS has remained clear this morning, and surface heating has allowed for destabilization, yielding 1000-1500 J/kg of MLCAPE as of 17Z, within a narrow corridor immediately ahead of the convective line. As surface heating/destabilization continue into the early afternoon, the ongoing convective activity may reintensify. Should this scenario occur, damaging wind gusts and severe hail would be possible, and a watch may be needed. However, detriments to this convective scenario include marginal deep-layer shear (perhaps nearing 30 kt of effective bulk shear) and the possibility of the MCS to outpace the instability corridor and remain sub-severe. Nevertheless, the area will continue being monitored for the possibility of a watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Increasing coverage/intensity of storms expected this afternoon in proximity to an outflow boundary. Large hail, damaging winds, and a tornado or two possible. Watch likely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Remnant outflow from a decaying MCS this morning is beginning to stall over southern Oklahoma as strong insolation has led to rapid modification and destabilization of the airmass. Temperatures near and south of the outflow boundary are in the upper 80s and lower 90s F and dew point temperatures remain quite high, in the 70sF. This has yielded MLCAPE approaching 4000 J/kg. Visible satellite shows developing cumulus that is at or nearing convective initiation, with one severe storm in Grady and McClain counties in Oklahoma. Given these convective trends, widespread convective development is anticipated in the next few hours. Storms that develop should organize into multicellular and supercellular structures initially, given effective bulk shear of 35-40 kt over the region (lessening with southern extent). As such, large hail and damaging wind gusts will be the primary threats, although a tornado or two could occur, particular for any storm that develops/crosses along the western portion of outflow boundary within the more favorably sheared environment. With time, storms should consolidate into a forward-propagating MCS and transition to primarily a damaging wind threat this evening.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few storms may produce isolated marginally severe hail across far eastern Colorado into western Kansas during the afternoon hours. A few cells closer to the upper-level low center may continue to produce cold air funnels and possibly a brief non-supercell tornado. Given the isolated and marginal extent of the severe threat, a WW issuance is not anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A 500-300 mb stacked low is currently traversing the central High Plains, advecting cold air atop a warming, modestly moist low-level atmosphere and promoting marginal instability across the area. Currently, over 500 J/kg MLCAPE and around 45 knots of effective bulk shear are present across the area, which may foster storm organization and at least transient mid-level rotation. With temperatures as cold as -19C at 500 mb noted over northeast Colorado, marginally severe hail may occur with any storm that can become organized and sustained. In addition, reports of funnel clouds have been received within the past few hours across portion of north-central Colorado. Appreciable amounts of mid-level vertically oriented vorticity is present given the proximity of the aforementioned upper-level low, and with at least a marginally buoyant airmass in place, additional cold air funnels may occur. Relatively higher 0-3km CAPE, supportive of vigorous low-level vorticity stretching in convective updrafts, is present across far east Colorado into Kansas. However, modest near-surface vertically oriented vorticity was noted (via mesoanalysis) in proximity of Adams, Washington and Morgan Counties area. Should an inflow dominant updraft become established in this area, a brief non-supercell tornado cannot be ruled out given the deep-layer vorticity rich environment. Still, the severe threat is expected to be limited enough in spatial/temporal extent to preclude a WW issuance.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated thunderstorms will continue to develop and move northeast with a risk for damaging gusts and perhaps hail. A watch is not anticipated, however trends will be monitored for indications of storm evolution into line segments with a subsequently greater coverage of severe potential.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorms have developed across the discussion area in an environment characterized by weak vertical wind shear but very strong/extreme surface-based instability, and substantial DCAPE in excess of 1000 J/kg. Additional daytime heating will further steepen low-level lapse rates, and the potential for damaging downburst winds will exist this afternoon with the stronger storms. Overall coverage is expected to remain isolated and therefore a watch is not anticipated. If the potential for greater organization into clusters or short line segments appears to increase, then a watch would be possible.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms have developed within an unstable airmass, posing a threat for a few damaging wind gusts. Watch possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite and radar shows a northwest to southeast oriented area of enhanced convective development, including a few pulse severe storms, over the region. Clear skies this morning allowed convective temperatures near 90 F to be exceeded amidst a residual moist airmass with dew point temperatures in the upper 60s and lower 70s F. Consequently, the airmass is quite unstable, with steep low-level lapse rates (near 8 C/km) and MLCAPE of 2000-2500 J/kg present over the region. However, deep-layer shear remains rather weak. Currently, storms are relatively isolated although becoming somewhat scattered. Uncertainty exists in whether storms will remain isolated or become more widespread. Given the aforementioned environmental indices, storms that mature will pose a threat for damaging wind gusts. Should the convective activity form into a few clusters or become more widespread, a watch may be needed for parts of the area.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for damaging winds continues across mainly eastern and southern portions of the watch area. With time, storms will move into a less favorable environment towards the Indiana-Ohio border and a downstream watch is not currently anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A linear convective system with a history of damaging winds and sporadic marginally severe hail continues to move northeast across southern/central IN at 1955Z. The environment immediately downstream remains favorable for a continued severe threat, with ample heating contributing to moderate surface-based buoyancy. With eastward extent towards the OH border, a substantial instability gradient exists that should result in an overall weakening trend of the northern portion of the line/bowing segment with time. As a result, a downstream watch is not anticipated across far southeast IN and southwest OH. ..Bunting.. 06/23/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe weather threat continues across the remaining valid portions of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 435. An areal extension may needed in the short term across portions of southern Arkansas and perhaps southern Illinois and western Kentucky.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Severe thunderstorms were in progress along an east/southeastward-moving linear convective system at 2035Z, with several reports of damaging winds received. The most intense portion of the line extended from southeast MO across central Arkansas, in an environment characterized by strong instability (MLCAPE in excess of 2000 J/kg) and 30-40 kts of southwesterly deep-layer shear. With a well-developed cold pool, the line should continue moving east/southeast this afternoon with a continued risk for damaging winds, with transient low-level circulations possible along the leading edge entering far southern Illinois and western Kentucky. A local watch extension in area may be needed in the short term across portions of southern Arkansas, where current line motion would take the convective line to the southern edge of the watch by around 2130Z. In addition, any northward development of the line across southeast MO would necessitate a local areal extension across southern IL and western KY north of the current watch boundary. ..Bunting.. 06/23/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: It is not certain that a new Severe Thunderstorm Watch will be needed for areas downstream of WW 435, although convective trends continue to be monitored.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An ongoing, yet broken line of storms persists from portions of the Indiana/Ohio border southward through central Kentucky. The downstream airmass is sufficiently unstable for storms to persist eastward - especially into eastern Kentucky where MUCAPE exceeds 3000 J/kg. One limiting factor for the overall severe threat remains weak deep shear, with wind fields generally less than 20-25 kts aloft and less than 5-10 kts at the surface. The overall severe threat will ultimately depend on mesoscale organization and further upscale growth of ongoing convection in tandem with maturing, merging cold pools. Convective evolution will continue to be monitored as storms approach the eastern extent of WW 435. ..Cook.. 06/23/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe threat may extend downstream of WW 433 from parts of western/central KY into middle TN, far northwest AL, northern and central MS and perhaps far southern AR/northern LA. Trends will be monitored but one or more additional watches may be needed in the next 1-2 hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The intensity of convection across WW 433 has decreased over the last 30-60 minutes in some area from western TN into eastern AR. Other areas, mainly western KY/southern IL and portions of southern AR, have increased in intensity. In the short term, WFOs PAH, MEG and LZK have addressed the continued strong wind threat will local aerial extensions as needed. Further south and east, the need for additional watch issuance still remains somewhat unclear. There is a well-established cold pool across AR behind the line with a well-defined meso high noted in surface analysis. Ahead of the line, a very warm and strongly unstable downstream airmass is in place across southern AR/northern LA into northern and central MS and portions of western and middle TN. This may allow for a continued sporadic damaging wind threat downstream of WW 433. That being said, effective shear diminishes rapidly with south and eastward extent and is not forecast to increase dramatically this evening, though a 30-40 kt southwesterly low level jet will overspread the region. VWP data from LZK does show evidence of a rear-inflow jet, but it is not overly strong or deep, at around 35-50 kt between .5-1.5 km. Further north, across western KY/southern IL, the line has been intensifying and surging eastward. This is likely being driven by the expansive cold pool across AR/MO as well as stronger deep flow in the vicinity of stronger forcing occurring with a weak shortwave impulse migrating across the mid-MS Valley region. This portion of the line may continue to produce damaging wind gusts and PAH has addressed this by expanding WW 433. A line of storms moved across parts of western/central KY early today, but recent observations show conditions have likely recovered somewhat across western portions of WFO LM

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated storms in the discussion area will pose a risk for hail/damaging wind gusts approaching severe thresholds for the next few hours, although a WW issuance is not anticipated at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Isolated to scattered convection has recently undergone an uptick in the OK/TX Panhandle and vicinity while a lone supercell tracks eastward very near I-70/HLC in central Kansas. These storms are likely aided by cooling aloft/ascent associated with a mid-level shortwave approaching the region from northeastern Colorado. Low-level shear is weak in this region, although 40-knot mid-level flow will likely contribute to some organization of updrafts as they migrate through an environment characterized by modestly steep lapse rates and high cloud bases. The longevity of this convection beyond sunset is in question, however, and will depend on any upscale growth of storms into a linear complex around the time that nocturnal boundary layer stabilization should be commencing. The sparse nature of the threat and uncertainty about persistence into the evening preclude a WW issuance for this activity, though trends will continue to be monitored. ..Cook.. 06/23/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A conditional wind and hail threat will persist this evening across portions of west-central Texas in the vicinity of the Rio Grande from near Del Rio, arcing southeastward to Dimmit County TX.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong storms have developed this evening across eastern Coahuila in Mexico. The left split from one supercell has weakened considerably as it tracked into Val Verde County northwest of DRT, but additional cells remain strong and probably severe across the Rio Grande/international border. Model guidance is quite inconsistent in the evolution of these storms into the late evening/overnight hours. Some guidance indicates storms will diminish and not pose a threat across west-central Texas while others bring the storms eastward and perhaps develop a bowing segment shifting east/southeast across parts of the Edwards Plateau and south-central TX. A very unstable airmass and 30-40 kt effective shear exists across the area, which is more than sufficient to maintain organized severe convection. However, midlevel temperatures are rather warm, leading to some capping to overcome in the presence of weak forcing. This could limit the threat overall as the boundary layer stabilizes with loss of daytime heating and preclude a greater severe threat. Given the marginal and uncertain/conditional nature of the threat, a watch is not expected at this time, though trends will continue to be monitored.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Damaging winds and hail will continue to be a concern as a line of storms surges southward toward the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex. A downstream watch may be needed into parts of central TX by 03z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A couple of lines of storms were affecting portions of northern TX this evening. A small bowing segment from Taylor into Stephens Counties produced a 53 kt gust at Abilene in the last hour with hail up to 1.75 inches also reported. Further to the north, convection extended from near Throckmorton County northeastward along the Red River. These storms have generally produced sub-severe gusts. However, a more unstable and moist downstream airmass ahead of a strengthening cold pool behind the line may be sufficient for the line to become better organized and surge more southward toward the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex over the next couple of hours. If the line can become better organized and intensify, expect that a corridor of greater damaging wind potential will reside along the I-35E and I-45 vicinity into the late evening/nighttime hours. If this occurs, a new watch downstream of WW 436 may be needed prior to 03z. ..Leitman.. 06/24/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated strong to severe wind gusts are possible the next couple of hours as storms track southeast across northwest OK toward central OK. A watch is not expected at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of storms that was tracking east/southeast across the OK/TX Panhandles earlier this evening has become better organized across northwest OK and the OK Mesonet station at Arnett recorded a 61 mph gust. Other OK Mesonet sites across northwest OK have measured 40-50 mph gusts. This increase in organization is probably due to increasing instability and boundary layer moisture with eastward extent. There is also likely some influence/increased ascent associated with a shortwave impulse ejecting with the midlevel trough across the central Plains, resulting in height falls and some cooling aloft. Convection may maintain organization as storms track to the southeast toward central and north-central OK at around 35-45 kt, and occasional strong/isolated severe wind gusts are possible the next couple of hours. While latest surface dewpoint trends and modest gains in MLCAPE suggest some airmass recovery of the residual cold pool from earlier day convection, low level lapse rates will continue to weaken as the boundary layer cools. In the absence of a stronger low level jet and as forcing for ascent decreases with time/southward extent, expect a gradual weakening trend of storms as they move toward north-central and central OK later this evening. As such, a watch is not expected at this time.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated damaging wind gusts remain possible across central and east-central TX.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convective line arcing from north-central LA into central TX continues to push eastward/southeastward at around 25 kt. Some increased forward progression has been noted in the past hour near the inflection point within the line over central TX. More backbuilding has also become evident along the far western portion of the line over the TX Hill Country. Over the last hour, wind gusts along the leading edge of the cold pool have only been around 25 kt. The strongest updrafts remain along the western, backbuilding portion of the line from Lampasas County into McLennan County. Highest severe threat currently exists in this area (and immediately downstream), where water loading within the strong updrafts could result in damaging downburst winds. ..Mosier.. 06/24/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated damaging wind gusts are possible as a weakening convective line moves across MS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Expansive convective line extends from northern MS southward across western MS and then back southwestward across central LA into central TX. North-south orientation of the line moving through western MS is aligned more favorably to the deep-shear vector than areas across LA or TX. Moderate low-level flow has also been gradually strengthening ahead of this line with the VAD profile from DGX now sampling 45 kt of southwesterly winds at 1 km. These factors have resulting in some localized surges within the line and a few strong wind gusts. A gust of 42 kt reported at HEZ as the line move through. Radar reflectivity trends suggest the line is weakening as it moves eastward. Even so, isolated damaging wind gusts will remain possible with this line as it continues eastward across much of MS. Marginal nature of the severe threat and overall weakening trend are expected to preclude the need for a watch.
